basics.name: Philopater Shenouda
basics.label: Junior Penetration Tester
basics.summary:
Information Technology graduate and Junior Penetration Tester currently training as a Penetration Tester at Classera, specializing in offensive security, vulnerability management, and risk analysis. Backed by intensive practical training from NTI, DEPI, and a prestigious cybersecurity diploma, I possess a proven track record in conducting structured web and network security assessments.

As a Bug Bounty Hunter on Bugcrowd and HackerOne, I leverage a true Red Team mindset to identify and responsibly disclose critical vulnerabilities, including IDOR, PII Breaches, Broken Access Control, XSS, and OTP Bypasses. Adept at building custom automation tools in Go and Python, as well as delivering clear, compliance-aligned remediation reports that secure complex enterprise environments.

projects.name: Argus-Digilians
projects.description: Autonomous AI pentesting framework automating end-to-end reconnaissance and vulnerability assessment in air-gapped environments.
highlights: Problem: Manual end-to-end penetration testing workflows are time-consuming and hard to reproduce consistently across engagements.
Solution: Built an autonomous agent framework on Python, LangChain, and local LLMs that parses dynamic target responses, executes contextual attack workflows, and generates security reports offline.

projects.name: PhilopaterSh URL
projects.description: Go-based tool for automated URL extraction and filtering, featuring enhanced performance and multiple data sources.
highlights: Problem: Existing URL extraction tools were often slow and missed endpoints by not integrating enough data sources, which hindered the reconnaissance phase of security assessments.
Solution: Developed a high-performance, concurrent tool in Go that aggregates data from multiple passive sources and applies intelligent filtering to extract unique URLs efficiently.

projects.name: PhilopaterSh Subdomain
projects.description: High-performance subdomain enumeration tool in Go integrating multiple passive data sources with concurrent discovery.
highlights: Problem: Fragmented subdomain data across different providers made it difficult to get a complete view of a target's attack surface during the discovery phase.
Solution: Built a Go-based tool that integrates various passive API sources with active concurrent discovery to provide a comprehensive and accurate list of subdomains.

projects.name: HCIA-Datacom V2 Review - GitBook
projects.description: Published GitBook study companion for the Huawei HCIA-Datacom V2.0 exam (H12-811): a full question bank rendered as a filterable, chapter-scoped review app plus a structured online book.
highlights: Problem: Exam dumps are flat, unfiltered, and painful to study from - hundreds of mixed-domain questions with no progress tracking, no chapter scoping, and no clean way to review on any device.

Solution: Built a reproducible content pipeline (immutable raw transcript -> build script -> validated question bank -> render) producing a GitBook edition and a self-contained review app with per-chapter filtering and a custom engine profile.
